transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… I’m here because I just haven’t been feeling like myself. Most days it feels like I’m stuck at the bottom of some dark hole, and even when I’m around people I know, I can’t really shake this heavy, hopeless feeling. I’m sorry, I don’t know if that’s the right way to explain it.
Can you describe how your mood is throughout the day? Is the low feeling present most of the time, or does it come and go?

It’s… pretty much there most of the day, I think. I try to act normal and I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but most days it feels like I’m down in this dark hole, and even when I’m around people I know, that heavy, hopeless feeling doesn’t really lift. Does that make sense?
How long have you been feeling this way? Have these feelings been present for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks or longer?

I think it’s been… longer than two weeks, yes. I don’t want to exaggerate it, but probably about a year and two months now. It started after that fall on the HVAC job, when I hurt my back, and then things just kind of started unraveling from there. Most days it’s been there, more or less.
Have you noticed that you don’t enjoy things as much as you used to, or that you’ve lost interest in activities you once found pleasurable?

Yeah… I mean, I guess I have noticed that. I used to really love hiking, and painting, and going to the makerspace to tinker with things. Even at work, figuring out a tricky install used to feel kind of satisfying.

Now I’ll look at my paint supplies or tools and just… stare at them. Or people will call about getting together or doing something, and I ignore it, not because I’m trying to be rude. It just doesn’t feel worth starting, if that makes sense. I know that probably sounds bad.
Have you found yourself feeling guilty or blaming yourself for things more than usual, or feeling like you’re not worth much?

Yeah… I mean, I try not to dwell on it, but yes. I do end up blaming myself a lot.

I keep telling myself I’m useless because I can’t work the way I used to, and then I’ll replay things over and over—apprentices I feel like I let down, bills I haven’t been able to pay—and it starts to feel like proof that I’ve ruined everything. I know that probably sounds harsh, but that’s where my head goes.
Have you been feeling more tired or low on energy lately, even when you're not doing much?

I… I don’t know if I’d call it more tired, exactly. I mean, I’m not doing a lot, so it feels silly to say I’m worn out.

Some days I guess I do feel kind of drained, but I haven’t really been keeping track. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Have you noticed any changes in your ability to think clearly, concentrate, or make decisions lately?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but stuff that used to be kind of automatic for me isn’t lately.

Like paperwork, or looking at repair diagrams… those used to be second nature, and now they kind of blur together. I’ll just sit there and not even be able to decide something dumb, like which form I should open first. It’s embarrassing to say out loud, but… is that what you mean?
Have you noticed that you've been moving more slowly than usual, or have trouble sitting still, like you're physically slowed down or restless?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I’m not pacing around or anything like that, it’s more the opposite.

Everything just takes me longer than it should. Getting up from the couch and walking to the kitchen feels like I’m moving through water, and even answering a simple question, I’ll just… lag. People have asked me if I’m okay because I guess I look slowed down. I feel a little embarrassed saying that, but yes, that’s been happening.
Have you had episodes like this before, where you felt down and lost interest in things, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean… I’ve had bad stretches before, like anyone does, but I don’t know if they were like this.

I guess this one feels different, or maybe I’m just noticing it more now. I don’t want to overstate it. Is it okay if I say I’m not sure?
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks, or is this the first time you've felt this way for this long?

I honestly don’t know. I’m trying to think back, and there were definitely times I felt pretty low, but I can’t say for sure it was two weeks like this, with losing interest too.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer. This feels like the first time it’s been this… long and noticeable, I guess. Is that okay to say?
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks, or is this the first time you've felt this way for this long?

I think… like I said, I can’t really pin down another time before this where it was clearly two weeks or more with both of those things.

I’ve had rough patches, sure, but I don’t know if they count the way you mean. This is the first one I can say has really been this long and hard to ignore. Does that answer it okay?
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks, or is this the first time you've felt this way for this long?

I’m sorry, I know I’m probably not giving you the clean answer you’re looking for. I really can’t say for sure that there was another time before this that lasted at least two weeks with both feeling down and not caring about things.

So… I guess I’d say this is the first time I can clearly recognize it being like this for this long. Is that okay?
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks?

I’m not sure, honestly. I’ve had periods before where I wasn’t doing great, but I can’t clearly remember one that was definitely at least two weeks with both feeling down and losing interest.

I don’t want to overstate it. This time is the one I can really point to.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks?

I guess… no, not that I can clearly say. I’ve had times before where I felt low or kind of off, but I don’t remember a stretch where it was definitely two weeks with both things like that.

I don’t want to give you the wrong answer just to make it fit. This current time is the only one I’m sure about.
Before this current period, have you ever had a time when you felt down and lost interest in things for a period of at least two weeks?

I don’t think so… at least not in a way I can honestly say for sure.

I know I’ve had rough patches before, but I can’t clearly point to one before this where it was both feeling down and losing interest for two weeks or more. This time is the one that stands out. Is that helpful?
